amendments.rr_assessment: Technically sound; incomplete: link replay before activation overwrites the password.
amendments.proposed: When MFA is required, POST /auth/invite/accept returns 200 {status: MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED, invite_context, expires_in} instead of 204. Precise state machine: (1) acceptance sets the password and leaves the account INVITED with no session; the invitation link stays live (72 h, 24 h for a sensitive invite) and is not marked used. (2) The context is an INVITE_CONTEXT enrollment challenge: single use, 15 minutes, confirmable only on PATH_B without a bearer token. (3) Replay: presenting the live link again sets a new password (replacing the earlier one), revokes every earlier context and PENDING factor, and issues a new context. (4) Abandonment: if the context expires unused, the account stays INVITED with the chosen password; a PENDING factor created by enroll/start remains inert (never authenticates, RR-A06) until the next acceptance or enrollment replaces it; sign-in is refused (INVITED) because the account is not active. (5) Activation happens only when the factor is confirmed; then the link is consumed. The two proofs of path B are possession of the invitation link and possession of the TOTP secret shown to whoever holds it; the password is chosen by the link holder.
amendments.reason: A 204 cannot carry the enrollment continuation required by 05 §11.3 path B.
amendments.code: Implemented as proposed (service.accept_invite, mfa.enroll_start/confirm with PATH_B binding). Replay behaviour described above is the current code: api/veda/platform/auth/service.py accept_invite accepts the live INVITE token again while the user is INVITED.

amendments.rr_assessment: Previous text REJECTED AS WRITTEN (OD-1): its security statement was false for MFA holders and reset-email volume. Replaced by this layered proposal.
amendments.existing: POST /auth/login 5/min per email; POST /auth/password/forgot 3/hour per email (08 §12); per-account throttles of 05 §4.
amendments.proposed: Layered limits. Known and unknown identifiers behave identically; no tier locks an account (except the certified 05 §4 lock for accounts without a factor), but a victim CAN be temporarily disrupted, as stated below. (1) Network limits: 10/min per client IP (IPv6 per /64) and 30/min per wide network (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) on login; 5/min and 20/min on forgot; 10/min per IP on MFA verify, MFA recovery, enroll confirm, email verify and email cancel. (2) Identifier-per-network limits: 5/min login and 3/hour forgot per (HMAC of the normalized email, /24 or /64), so a third party cannot rate-limit the victim from every network (IR-23). (3) Account budget across all networks: 10 password failures in a sliding 15 minutes → every attempt for that identifier needs a solved Turnstile challenge, from any network; 20 → attempts are also spaced by an escalating interval (2 s doubling to 30 s; 429 + Retry-After). The correct password is not evaluated without the challenge (closes the MFA_REQUIRED oracle). A successful sign-in does not reset the budget. (4) Aggregate: 200 failures across all identifiers in 5 minutes → challenge for every sign-in while the window holds. (5) MFA: 10 MFA, recovery or enrollment-confirmation failures per account in 15 minutes → MFA throttled 15 minutes (05 §4). (6) Reset emails: at most 3 per account per hour across all networks; further requests get the identical 202 and send nothing. (7) The certified per-(account, network) throttle and 5-network global lock for accounts without a factor are unchanged. Trusted proxy: CF-Connecting-IP is believed only from configured peers, each at most /24 or /64; otherwise the TCP peer is the client. Privacy: limiter keys and events carry an HMAC of the normalized email, never the address. Cardinality: in-process tables capped at 50 000 keys each (expired entries evicted first, then the oldest); one application process (OPS-010).
amendments.reason: Keep IR-23 (no victim lock-out from a third party's network) while restoring a cross-network bound on password guessing for every account, including MFA holders, and on reset-email volume.
amendments.code: Implemented at this commit: api/veda/platform/auth/throttle.py (account budget, aggregate, reset cap, bounded tables), api/veda/kernel/ratelimit.py (wide-network and hashed identifier keys), api/veda/platform/auth/service.py (login and forgot), api/veda/platform/auth/routes.py (endpoint limits), api/veda/config.py (trusted-proxy prefix bound).
amendments.security: Not claimed: per-account throttling alone does not bound password guessing (the certified lock exempts factor holders); the bound comes from tiers (1)–(4) together. Distributed guessing per account: ≤ 10 unchallenged attempts per 15 minutes, then one solved challenge per attempt, then ≤ 1 attempt per 30 s; an attacker with a human or paid challenge-solving budget can still guess slowly. Victim disruption that remains possible: (a) FC-05 — a third party can send the three reset emails early in an hour; each new link invalidates the previous one and links expire after 30 minutes, so the victim can be without a usable reset link for roughly half of every hour while the attack continues (the victim can still sign in with the password; an administrator can issue a reset); (b) while an identifier is escalated the victim must solve a challenge and may wait up to 30 s per attempt. Turnstile/provider outage (FC-A06): escalation lasts as long as failures keep arriving (sliding 15-minute window), and a challenge cannot be verified during an outage, so an escalated identifier cannot sign in for the whole outage-under-attack plus up to 15 minutes after failures stop. This is fail-closed and not bounded by 15 minutes under a sustained attack. Identifiers that are not escalated are unaffected; aggregate escalation during an outage refuses every password sign-in until the aggregate window drains. Accuracy (FC-A05): the budget check and record are separate steps, so concurrent in-flight attempts can exceed a threshold by the number of requests in flight.

amendments.rollback: Remove tiers (3), (4) and (6): the MFA-holder guessing gap of RR-04 returns. Not recommended.

amendments.proposed: A deleted Founder keeps FOUNDER protection and roles and is restored only by FOUNDER_STATUS_CHANGE status=RESTORE: requested by one eligible Founder, approved in-app by a second, distinct eligible Founder (requester and target can never approve; one decision per request). The account returns DISABLED and FOUNDER-protected; reactivation is a separate FOUNDER_STATUS_CHANGE ACTIVE. Eligibility is checked at request, approval and execution under the governance lock; at execution the target must still be deleted and its address free, otherwise the request FAILS. Neither break-glass channel (single-Founder or custodian) may carry a restore — it is outside the approved break-glass policy (SECOND_FOUNDER_REQUIRED). POST /users/{id}/restore applies G3 and G11 and answers 403 FOUNDER_PROTECTED with a FOUNDER_GOVERNANCE_BYPASS_BLOCKED event for a Founder. Last-Founder invariants are re-checked (a restore never reduces the Founder count). Precise behaviour (FC-A10, FC-A11, FC-A12): the custodian CLI cannot address a deleted account at all — it refuses the restore as an unknown target and records no BREAK_GLASS_REQUESTED FAILURE event; SECOND_FOUNDER_REQUIRED is the service-level answer for in-app and direct callers. The FOUNDER_ACTION_REQUESTED/EXECUTED/FAILED events carry action FOUNDER_STATUS_CHANGE; RESTORE appears in the request payload (status) and in the FOUNDER_TRANSITION event. A restored and later reactivated Founder signs in with the password and MFA factor held before deletion (deletion revoked sessions and links, not credentials); the owner may require a FOUNDER_MFA_RESET and a password reset as part of reactivation.

amendments.existing: 06 §7.4 re-evaluates G11 and G9 when a STANDARD request is decided and executed; a started email change (05 §8.6) completes on verification with no further check.
amendments.proposed: Governance classes: STANDARD_CONTROL < DUAL_CONTROL (holds a sensitive permission) < FOUNDER_GOVERNANCE. Withdrawal happens on GRANT_FOUNDER and on user-level role or permission changes that raise the class: open STANDARD requests are cancelled (Founder) and a pending email proposal not requested by the owner is cleared with its links (EMAIL_CHANGE_CANCELLED with reason and class transition). A class raised in any other way — a role DEFINITION gaining a sensitive permission — does not withdraw anything: the proposal is only BLOCKED at verification while the class stays raised, and if the change is reverted the old link verifies again (FC-08). At verification the proposal's authorising class (self, direct administrator, EMAIL_CHANGE request, FOUNDER_EMAIL_CHANGE request) is recomputed against the current class; weaker authorisation or a DISABLED account fails closed (EMAIL_TOKEN_INVALID; EMAIL_CHANGE_VERIFIED FAILURE; FOUNDER_GOVERNANCE_BYPASS_BLOCKED for Founders). Not covered (FC-A09): administrator-issued password-reset links and MFA-enrollment links survive a promotion to Founder; they are delivered only to the account's own verified address. Founder-level and break-glass requests re-validate the target at execution.
